device.name: Enphase Envoy
device.notes: Enphase Envoy gateways expose a local REST API on port 80 for solar production and inverter telemetry. Some endpoints are readable locally, while newer firmware gates selected endpoints behind token-based authentication. Discovery uses the Enphase-specific mDNS service and the serialnum TXT record is the stable identity.

issued_to_client: JWT bearer token from the Enphase entrez service (firmware 7+)
credentials.notes: Older firmware used HTTP digest auth with an installer password derived from the serial number; current firmware requires a cloud-issued token that expires, which makes even 'local' telemetry cloud-dependent for renewal. Cache the token and record its expiry.

factory_reset.effect: Not documented in this project. Re-provisioning is normally done in place from the gateway's own UI rather than by resetting it.

steps.action: Consult the model's installation manual; a full reset can de-commission the PV site and should not be done casually.

methods.description: Ethernet or Enphase powerline (PLC) to the router; no wireless provisioning needed.

steps.action: Connect the gateway to the LAN and power it.

methods.description: For wireless installs the gateway hosts a temporary access point and serves its own configuration UI, where the installer selects the home network. The AP name is derived from the gateway serial.

softap.passphrase_source: Derived from the gateway serial number; printed in the installation documentation.

steps.action: Press the AP Mode button on the gateway to start the setup AP.
Join the Envoy_* network and open the gateway's configuration page.
steps.notes: Address and passphrase derivation are vendor-documented; confirm against the unit before relying on them.

steps.action: Select the home network and apply.

setup.notes: The Envoy is commissioned by an installer rather than unboxed by an owner, so its onboarding is a web UI on the gateway itself rather than an app protocol. The part that matters for local-first consumers is not the WiFi join but the authentication change: firmware 7 and later require a JWT obtained from Enphase's entrez service for local endpoints that used to be open or digest-authenticated.

rejoin.notes: Network settings can be changed from the gateway's local web UI while it is still reachable, which is the supported way to move it to a new router.

http_endpoints.description: Live solar production and consumption data. Discovery scripts can probe this path after mDNS resolution.
http_endpoints.name: Production

http_endpoints.description: Per-inverter production telemetry; may require token authentication on newer firmware.
http_endpoints.name: Inverter Production

http_endpoints.description: Envoy gateway information, including identifiers and firmware details where available.
